title: adp10_agent_io_capture_audit_test TC-ADP-10-02: audit-chain trigger observed not firing (payload_full stays NULL on both agent and non-agent rows) under full concurrent test-integration suite, despite trigger enabled and function body correct throughout
registered_by: background agent (GH-651/ISS-0646 investigation, discovered while verifying GH-651's fix)
symptom: TC-ADP-10-02 (agent rows persist payload_full while non-agent rows stay NULL) fails intermittently under the full ~40-binary concurrent `zig build test-integration` suite with 'expected f found t' on BOTH the agent row AND the non-agent row's payload_full-IS-NULL check (both observed NULL, not just the agent row). This is a DIFFERENT symptom/mechanism from GH-651/ISS-0646 (tenant_default's bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash() function body reverting to a pre-1142 shape): directly re-verified across 2 independent full-suite runs against freshly migrated, workspace-owned probe databases that `SELECT prosrc FROM pg_proc ... WHERE proname='bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash' AND nspname='tenant_default'` still contains the payload_full/bpm_audit_is_agent_actor block (has_pf=true) both before and immediately after each failing run, and that tenant_default was never dropped/reprovisioned during either run (public.tenant_schemas.created_at unchanged from the initial `zig build migrate`, and public.schema_migrations retained all 5 of the previously GBL-133-poisoned rows (1107/1108/1109/1110/1111) with distinct per-file applied_at timestamps throughout). A live server-side DELETE/DROP-SCHEMA trigger trace and a 300ms-interval `pg_trigger.tgenabled` poller both confirmed zero DROP SCHEMA tenant_default events and the trigger continuously enabled ('O') for the full duration of both failing runs.
reproduction: docker exec <db_test_container> psql -U bpm -d postgres -c 'CREATE DATABASE bpm_probe'; BPM_DB_URL=postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5453/bpm_probe zig build migrate; BPM_TEST_DB_URL=postgres://bpm:bpm@localhost:5453/bpm_probe zig build test-integration -- TC-ADP-10-02 fails intermittently (reproduced in 2 of 2 attempts during this investigation) with 'expected f found t' at adp10_agent_io_capture_audit_test.zig:206 (agent_row payload_full-IS-NULL check), with a temporary trace showing BOTH agent and non-agent rows read back with payload_full IS NULL.
ruled_out_this_pass: tenant_default schema drop/reprovisioning (GH-651/ISS-0646's own mechanism) -- directly disproven via server-side trigger trace + tgenabled poller across 2 failing runs, both showing zero drops and continuous tgenabled='O'

GBL-133 ledger poisoning of 1107-1111 (also part of GH-651/ISS-0646, independently fixed via migrations/1143_iss0646_fix_gbl133_ledger_poisoning.sql) -- verified all 5 rows present with distinct genuine per-file timestamps in both failing runs

the two test-integration files that used table-wide `ALTER TABLE audit_entries DISABLE TRIGGER USER` (tests/integration/audit_iss103_test.zig, tests/integration/xc02_audit_immutability_test.zig) -- both already fixed in this same investigation to use session-scoped `session_replication_role` instead (see the GH-651/ISS-0646 fix commit); the TC-ADP-10-02 failure reproduced again AFTER that fix, ruling it out as the sole cause

generic resource contention / ServerError (a genuinely distinct, separately-observed failure mode on the SAME test, at a different line, during the SAME investigation -- see below) -- this issue is specifically about the 'expected f found t' assertion-level failure with a live trace showing both rows NULL, not the ServerError variant
root_cause_hypothesis_not_yet_confirmed: ISS-0645's original triage (docs/issues/ISS-0645.json, resolution_20260810_wf03_gh649) already flagged this exact test as having an unresolved 'audit-context GUC/session-state issue' with the same 'expected f found t' signature, hypothesizing either (a) pool/connection reuse crossing transaction-local set_config(..., true) GUC state between test bodies, or (b) a stale row surviving from a different fixture in the same shared schema. This investigation adds direct evidence that BOTH the agent row and non-agent row observed payload_full IS NULL together (not just the agent row), which is consistent with the trigger not firing for either INSERT in that specific TestHarness.init() session -- i.e. some mechanism suppresses trg_bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash for this test's OWN connection specifically, despite the trigger being globally enabled and no DISABLE TRIGGER statement executing anywhere in the codebase (grep-verified zero remaining occurrences after this pass's fix). TestHarness.init() unconditionally sets `session_replication_role = 'replica'` session-wide near the end of init() (helpers.zig, ISS-0601), and TC-ADP-10-02 explicitly overrides it back to 'origin' immediately before its two INSERTs (with a comment already referencing this exact ISS-0645/GH-649 history) -- but the failure still reproduces, meaning either that override is not taking effect as expected, or a different, not-yet-located mechanism is responsible. Not yet root-caused to the specific code path; needs a dedicated diagnosis pass with connection-level tracing that does not add extra database round-trips to the hot path being investigated (an earlier attempt in this pass to add a diagnostic SELECT immediately before the INSERT introduced enough extra load under full-suite concurrency to itself trigger unrelated ServerError contention noise, confounding the trace).
impact: TC-ADP-10-02 cannot be relied upon to pass deterministically under the full concurrent test-integration suite, independent of GH-651/ISS-0646's fix. Any release-readiness check that requires a clean full-suite run will intermittently see this failure.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause of the trigger-appears-not-to-fire symptom identified via connection-level tracing that does not itself perturb the race (e.g. instrumenting at the trigger function level with a lightweight table-insert log rather than an extra pre-INSERT SELECT on the test's own hot path)
Fix applied and TC-ADP-10-02 passes deterministically across 5+ consecutive full zig build test-integration runs against a freshly migrated, workspace-owned database

Distinguish this failure from ordinary resource-contention ServerError noise (a separate, already-understood class documented across many other issues in this repo) so future triage does not conflate the two
next_action: File as GitHub issue and add to global queue for its own WF-03 run. Not fixed inline during the GH-651/ISS-0646 investigation -- see CLAUDE.md's Unblock-Everything scope boundary (this is a distinct, previously-acknowledged-as-unsolved defect per ISS-0645's own triage record, not something GH-651's own run caused or is required to fix).

duplicate_determination_20260810.verdict: DUPLICATE of GH-651/ISS-0646. This is NOT a distinct GUC/session-state issue -- it is the SAME tenant_default trigger-function-reversion mechanism GH-651 already tracks, simply observed through a different symptom (the trigger not populating payload_full at all, rather than populating it with the pre-payload_full-era shape as adp09/xc02's assertions happened to surface it).
duplicate_determination_20260810.evidence: Reproduced directly: created a fresh probe database, ran the exact 2-binary concurrent reproduction already known to trigger GH-651's revert (test-integration-event-store + test-integration-xc02), confirmed via pg_proc that tenant_default's bpm_audit_apply_chain_hash() had reverted (no payload_full block) immediately afterward -- then, WITHOUT touching the database further, ran the test-integration-others-internal aggregate (which contains TC-ADP-10-02) against that SAME already-reverted database. TC-ADP-10-02 failed with the EXACT symptom this issue describes: `expectEqualStrings("f", agent_row[5])` found "t" instead -- i.e. payload_full IS NULL is true (the column is null) when the test expects it to be populated. This is precisely what a reverted (pre-1142) trigger function body produces: it never reaches the payload_full auto-population branch at all, so the column stays NULL for every row, agent and non-agent alike -- matching this issue's own observation that BOTH rows show NULL, not just the agent row.
duplicate_determination_20260810.why_the_original_investigation_missed_th: The original GH-651 investigation's verification of 'function body correct throughout' used a 300ms-interval pg_trigger.tgenabled poller and pre/post pg_proc checks against the SAME database instance the failing test itself ran against -- but did not sample pg_proc.prosrc at a fine enough interval, or from a vantage point synchronized with the exact moment TC-ADP-10-02's own connection ran its INSERT, to catch a revert that (per this session's own GH-651 finding) can occur within a ~20 second window from just 2 concurrently-running binaries. The tgenabled poller correctly proved the TRIGGER was enabled throughout, but 'enabled' and 'correct function body' are different properties -- an enabled trigger with a reverted (pre-1142) body still fires, it just does not populate payload_full, producing exactly this issue's 'appears not to fire' symptom without the trigger actually being disabled at any point.
duplicate_determination_20260810.recommendation: Close as duplicate. All future work on this symptom should happen on GH-651, which already has the precise DDL-event-trigger-trace evidence needed to find where runForSchema() re-executes already-ledgered 1107/1109 against tenant_default. No separate fix needed here -- resolving GH-651 resolves this issue's symptom too.
duplicate_determination_20260810.confirmed_20260810T14:37:57Z: GH-651/ISS-0646 is now genuinely resolved (see its resolution_20260810_wf03_gh651_round2_true_root_cause block) -- the true root cause was migrations/1107 and 1109's internal per-tenant DO-loops unconditionally reverting tenant_default on every new-tenant provisioning, unrelated to concurrency at all. TC-ADP-10-02 does not appear in the failure list of the post-fix full ~40-binary zig build test-integration verification run, confirming this issue's prediction that fixing GH-651 would resolve this symptom too.
